payload.title: Count of the Levite families

aliases: the God of our Lord Jesus Christ
him who sits on the throne
payload.name: God / Yahweh, the Father and God of Israel
payload.note: The one God, creator and speaker of the Old Testament and the Father of Jesus Christ in the New Testament; distinct from Jesus in every entry.

stages.label: God the Father (radiance and cloud)

quotes.quote: Heaven is my throne, and the earth is my footstool.
Behold, Yahweh rides on a swift cloud, and comes to Egypt.

stages.text: God the Father: no human face or body; presence shown only as radiance, cloud and fire. A brilliant white-gold light without a source, veiled by a dense, slowly moving cloud, with a fire-like glow at its heart. Throne-light and footstool-earth implied at the edges, never a figure seated in it.

payload.name: Moses
payload.note: Israel's lawgiver and leader who led the people out of Egypt, received the law at Sinai and is named across the Old and New Testament divisions as the same individual, distinguished only by the sections in which he appears or is mentioned.

stages.label: Moses, elder

quotes.quote: Moses was eighty years old, and Aaron eighty-three years old, when they spoke to Pharaoh.

stages.text: Moses: an old man of about eighty; lean, weathered build; brown skin darkened by desert sun; white hair and a long white beard; deep-set, steady eyes and lined brow; a plain undyed linen tunic belted at the waist with a long dark-brown wool cloak; he carries a wooden shepherd's staff of dark acacia wood, and only he bears the rod of God.

stages.label: Moses, infant

quotes.quote: The woman conceived and bore a son. When she saw that he was a fine child, she hid him three months.

stages.text: Moses: a newborn infant; soft smooth skin; a small round face; a little dark hair; wrapped in plain linen cloth and laid in a woven reed basket sealed with bitumen and pitch; no beard, no staff, no adult clothing.

stages.label: Moses, adult

quotes.quote: But when he was forty years old, it came into his heart to visit his brothers, the children of Israel.

stages.text: Moses: a man of about forty; lean, strong, well-proportioned build; brown skin; short dark hair and a close-trimmed dark beard; alert, sober face; a knee-length undyed linen tunic with a dark woven wool cloak of brown and grey pinned at the shoulder; he carries a plain wooden shepherd's staff.

payload.name: Aaron, brother of Moses
payload.note: Moses' older brother and first high priest, in Exodus and in Numbers (census, offerings, death on Mount Hor); the same man across both divisions.

stages.label: Aaron, the first high priest

quotes.quote: Amram took Jochebed his father’s sister to himself as wife; and she bore him Aaron and Moses.
Of the blue, purple, and scarlet, they made finely worked garments for ministering in the holy place, and made the holy garments for Aaron
Aaron cast down his rod before Pharaoh and before his servants, and it became a serpent.

stages.text: Aaron: man in his eighties, older brother of Moses; lean, upright build; olive-brown skin; short grey-streaked beard and close-cropped hair; calm, grave face with deep-set eyes. Signature outfit: a long white linen tunic with a blue robe, a woven ephod of blue, purple and scarlet, a breastplate, and a linen headband. Props: none carried alone; the rod of the Exodus is sometimes held.

payload.name: The Levites
payload.note: The tribe of Levi serving in the tabernacle and carrying its furnishings in Numbers.

stages.label: The Levites

quotes.quote: The Levites purified themselves from sin, and they washed their clothes
from twenty-five years old and upward they shall go in to wait on the service
They shall carry the tabernacle and all its furnishings

stages.text: The Levites: men from twenty-five years old upward, of mature working age; sturdy, unhurried build from carrying the tabernacle frames and furnishings; olive-brown skin; short dark hair and close-trimmed beard; calm, dignified features. Signature outfit: a plain undyed linen tunic belted at the waist with a cloak of undyed wool, washed clean; a wooden carrying pole across the shoulders.

aliases: the mountain that might be touched
payload.name: Horeb/Mount Sinai
payload.note: The single mountain of God where the law and covenant are given; all listed entries (Exodus, Leviticus, Numbers, Deuteronomy, 1 Kings, Malachi, Hebrews) refer to the same mountain under the names Horeb, Sinai, God's mountain, referenced across divisions.

stages.label: Horeb/Mount Sinai

quotes.quote: All of Mount Sinai smoked, because Yahweh descended on it in fire
You shall set bounds to the people all around
the cloud covered it six days
The mountain burned with fire to the heart of the sky, with darkness, cloud, and thick darkness.

stages.text: Horeb/Mount Sinai: a single steep granite mountain rising from a stark desert wilderness of rock and sand; its lower slopes are broken boulders and gravel, its upper peak sharp and dark, with a cloud-wrapped summit. The base is marked by a rocky plain where the people camp, bounded by stones. No vegetation beyond scattered desert shrub; the mountain has no buildings.

aliases: the door of the Tent of Meeting
the court of the Tent of Meeting
payload.name: the tabernacle (portable sanctuary)
payload.note: The one portable sanctuary of the wilderness, described in Exodus 25-40 and referred to as the Tent of Meeting in Leviticus and Numbers; all three entries are the same place.

stages.label: The tabernacle (portable sanctuary)

quotes.quote: made the tabernacle with ten curtains of fine twined linen, blue, purple, and scarlet. They made them with cherubim
He made curtains of goats’ hair for a covering over the tabernacle.
He made the boards for the tabernacle, twenty boards for the south side southward.
the sockets around the court, the sockets of the gate of the court, all the pins of the tabernacle

stages.text: The tabernacle: a portable sanctuary of a rectangular tent of fine twined linen curtains in blue, purple and scarlet woven with cherubim, over a covering of goats' hair and rams' skins, stretched over upright acacia boards overlaid with gold, set in silver sockets and held by gold-covered bars, enclosed by a court of white linen hangings on bronze pillars.

payload.title: Israel encamps by the sea; Pharaoh pursues; fear

aliases: those who came out of Egypt
payload.name: The Israelite people (the children of Israel)
payload.note: The collective Israelite nation across Exodus through Malachi and Hebrews, one body whose different portrayals (marching nation, assembly, covenant people, judged northern kingdom, returned community, wilderness generation) are all the same people; distinguish only from the returned community of Nehemiah in the note by the Judah/Jerusalem setting, but these are the same people.

stages.label: The Israelite people

quotes.quote: Now these are the names of the sons of Israel, who came into Egypt
You shall tell the children of Israel this
So they shall put my name on the children of Israel; and I will bless them.

stages.text: The Israelite people: a typical member is an adult of mixed age, from youth to middle years, of sturdy and weathered build shaped by desert travel and field labour. Skin is warm olive-brown, hair dark and kept short or tied back, with full beards on men. Faces are calm and steady with dark eyes. Signature outfit: a plain undyed woven linen tunic in ochre or cream with a wool cloak in earth brown.

aliases: Pharaoh (king of Egypt who did not know Joseph)
payload.name: Pharaoh of the Exodus (oppressor of Israel)
payload.note: The unnamed king of Egypt in Exodus who enslaves Israel, hardens his heart against Moses and suffers the plagues; the same king recalled in Deuteronomy and cited in Romans 9:17 as the one raised up to show God's power.

stages.label: Pharaoh of the Exodus

quotes.quote: The king of Egypt called for the midwives, and said to them
Pharaoh’s heart was hardened, and he didn’t listen to them

stages.text: Pharaoh of the Exodus: man in his fifties, tall and broad-shouldered, dark brown skin; close-cropped hair under a blue-and-gold nemes headcloth, and a short trimmed false beard of the royal style; calm, hard features with heavy-lidded eyes and a firm mouth. Signature outfit: white linen kilt with a pleated gold-edged apron, broad gold collar, and red-and-gold royal sash. Signature props: gold crook and flail of royal office, carried alone.

payload.name: the Egyptians
payload.note: The Egyptian people, officers and magicians in Exodus who oppress Israel and suffer the plagues; distinguished from the Egyptian magicians of Genesis and from the Chaldeans of Babylon.

stages.label: the Egyptians

quotes.quote: The Egyptians ruthlessly made the children of Israel serve,
They also, the magicians of Egypt, did the same thing with their enchantments.

stages.text: the Egyptians: adults of middle age, broad-shouldered and strong from labour and rank, with warm brown skin and close-cropped black hair, clean-shaven men with short wigs or bare heads, dignified and grave of face. Signature outfit: a pleated white linen kilt or wrap-tunic with a linen cloak in ochre and blue. Signature props: none carried alone; officers may bear a staff of office.

payload.name: Red Sea
payload.note: The sea in Exodus that parts for Israel and closes over Pharaoh's army; distinct from the other seas by its setting in the exodus narrative.

stages.label: Red Sea

quotes.quote: Moses stretched out his hand over the sea, and Yahweh caused the sea to go back by a strong east wind all night
the waters were a wall to them on their right hand and on their left.
You shall encamp opposite it by the sea.

stages.text: Red Sea: a wide, deep arm of open water between desert shores, its surface dark blue-green under wind. Sand dunes and low reddish cliffs line the coast; scattered tamarisk and palms grow at the water's edge. Bare rock outcrops and shallow wadis run down to the shore, and a distant fortified town sits on the northern ridge.

payload.name: The wilderness (Exodus route)
payload.note: The desert stretches Israel travels from Egypt through Shur, Sin and Marah, with manna, quail and water miracles; the same wilderness as the Psalms and Amos references.

stages.label: The wilderness (Exodus route)

quotes.quote: they went out into the wilderness of Shur; and they went three days in the wilderness, and found no water.
on the surface of the wilderness was a small round thing, small as the frost on the ground.
in a dry and weary land, where there is no water.

stages.text: The wilderness: a vast arid tableland of pale sand, gravel plains and dark rock outcrops rising to bare mountains, scattered with thorn scrub and sparse grasses in the wadis. Tents and camp-circles mark the encampments; a distant mountain, Sinai, rises above the plain. Dry riverbeds, stone wells and rock fissures suggest hidden water.

payload.title: The city's ruin, the priests' guilt and Edom's doom

payload.name: Zion
payload.note: Personified city of Jerusalem as a mourning widow and captive princess, speaking in the first person in Lamentations 1 and 2; distinct from the collective people of Judah and Jerusalem.

stages.label: Zion, the mourning city-woman

quotes.quote: She has become as a widow, who was great among the nations!
All her gates are desolate. Her priests sigh.
They have clothed themselves with sackcloth. The virgins of Jerusalem hang down their heads to the ground.

stages.text: Zion: a woman of middle years, dignified and grieving, with dark hair bound low and partly veiled, olive skin darkened by ash and dust. Her features are worn and sorrowful. She wears a plain undyed linen robe under a dark sackcloth mantle of brown and grey, with a torn hem. She carries no regalia.

payload.name: Children of Zion (Lamentations)
payload.note: Infants and children who faint in the streets or beg for bread in Lamentations.

stages.label: Children of Zion

quotes.quote: the young children and the infants swoon in the streets of the city
The precious sons of Zion, comparable to fine gold
The tongue of the nursing child clings to the roof of his mouth for thirst.

stages.text: Children of Zion: young boys and girls aged about four to twelve, with slight thin builds worn down by hunger; olive to brown skin dulled with dust; dark hair cropped short or tied back; large dark eyes and sunken cheeks. Plain undyed linen or wool tunics belted with cord, faded to grey-brown, bare feet dusty. Signature prop: a small clay jar or pitcher held close.

payload.name: The priests of Jerusalem
payload.note: Collective body of priests in Lamentations who are killed in the sanctuary; a group, not an individual.

stages.label: Priests of Jerusalem

quotes.quote: Her priests sigh.
Should the priest and the prophet be killed in the sanctuary of the Lord?

stages.text: The priests of Jerusalem: men of middle to later years, lean and dignified, with dark-brown skin, short dark hair and a neatly kept beard flecked with grey. Calm, grave faces marked by sorrow. Signature outfit: a white linen priestly tunic and a linen headband, with a blue-violet cloak over the shoulders. Carry only a bronze censer.

payload.name: Prophets of Jerusalem
payload.note: The prophets of Jerusalem who gave false visions and are blamed for the city's fall, as portrayed in Lamentations.

stages.label: Prophets of Jerusalem

quotes.quote: her prophets find no vision from Yahweh
the sins of her prophets and the iniquities of her priests

stages.text: Prophets of Jerusalem: men in middle age, lean and weathered, with dark skin tanned by sun and a sturdy build. Short dark beards, hair cropped at the neck, deep-set attentive eyes. Signature outfit: a long undyed linen tunic with a dull ochre wool cloak. Each carries a plain wooden staff.

payload.name: The enemies (Jerusalem's foreign adversaries)
payload.note: Collective invaders and persecutors who destroy Jerusalem in Lamentations; a human/national group, not the divine accuser, so keep separate from Satan.

stages.label: The enemies (Jerusalem's foreign adversaries)

quotes.quote: Her adversaries have become the head. Her enemies prosper

stages.text: The enemies: adult men of the Mesopotamian and neighbouring Levantine peoples, aged twenty to fifty, lean and hardened by campaign. Skin weathered tan to olive-brown. Hair short or bound back, beards trimmed close. Stern, watchful faces. Typical dress: a sleeveless or short-sleeved tunic of undyed wool with a leather belt, a bronze-scaled or leather armour, and a dusty brown cloak. Colours: ochre, rust and iron-grey. Carries a spear or curved sword; no other props.

aliases: the city of my fathers' tombs
payload.name: Jerusalem
payload.note: The capital city of Judah (also called Jebus, David's city, the holy city, Zion as city in some books); the city itself, distinct from the hill/mountain of Zion as a place of Yahweh's dwelling.

stages.label: Jerusalem

quotes.quote: they buried him in David's city
a breach was made in the city

stages.text: Jerusalem: a walled city on a steep limestone ridge of the Judean hills, terraces of olive and fig trees falling into deep valleys. Stone and mud-brick houses with flat roofs crowd the slopes; a fortified citadel of the stronghold of Zion stands on the high ground. Massive city walls with gates, and above the city the temple mount crowned by a stone-built temple of Yahweh.

payload.name: The streets of the city
payload.note: Streets and roads where the children faint, the dead lie and the blind wander.

stages.label: The streets of the city

quotes.quote: The roads to Zion mourn, because no one comes to the solemn assembly.
All her gates are desolate.
The stones of the sanctuary are poured out at the head of every street.

stages.text: The streets of the city: narrow, unpaved or rough-stoned lanes winding between low flat-roofed houses of mud brick and dressed limestone, with broken walls and ruined doorways. Dust and ash lie thick; some stones of the sanctuary and fallen gold-toned debris lie at the corners. Sparse dry scrub grows in cracks, and gates stand desolate at the end of roads leading up toward Zion.

aliases: the house which is called by my name
the tent of the daughter of Zion
the house of Yahweh of Armies
payload.name: Yahweh's house in Jerusalem (the temple)
payload.note: The one Jerusalem temple (Yahweh's house, the sanctuary on Mount Moriah) across all references, from Solomon's building through repair, destruction and rebuilding; construction and ruin are later appearance stages, not separate places.

stages.label: Solomon's temple on Mount Moriah

quotes.quote: The house, when it was under construction, was built of stone prepared at the quarry
Within the inner sanctuary was twenty cubits in length, and twenty cubits in width, and twenty cubits in its height.
He overlaid the floor of the house with gold, inside and outside.
Also he made before the house two pillars thirty-five cubits high
He set the sea on the right side of the house eastward and toward the south.

stages.text: Yahweh's house in Jerusalem: a stone temple of finished ashlar on Mount Moriah, roofed with cedar beams, its inner sanctuary panelled in cedar and overlaid with pure gold. Carved cherubim, palm and open flowers cover the doors and walls. Before the house stand two great bronze pillars and a huge bronze molten sea on twelve oxen. Courts of stone surround it, with olive and cypress trees, and the walled city of Jerusalem rises beyond.

aliases: Edom in the land of Uz
payload.name: The wilderness and exile
payload.note: The Lamentations setting of captivity, pursuit and hiding where the exiles dwell or are hunted; a different place from the Egyptian prison despite the shared alias 'the dungeon'.

stages.label: The wilderness and exile

quotes.quote: She dwells among the nations. She finds no rest.
They have cut off my life in the dungeon, and have cast a stone on me.
The breath of our nostrils, the anointed of Yahweh, was taken in their pits

stages.text: The wilderness and exile: arid highland and dry steppe under a pale sky, scattered with stony ravines, cisterns cut into rock, and low flat-roofed mud-brick dwellings and walled settlements of foreign towns. Sparse thorn scrub and dry grass, a few gnarled terebinths, and distant ruined walls of a broken city on the horizon.

payload.title: Remnant returns and approach of invaders

payload.name: Isaiah son of Amoz
payload.note: Prophet who advises Hezekiah; the same prophet across Isaiah, 2 Kings and 2 Chronicles.

stages.label: Isaiah son of Amoz

quotes.quote: The vision of Isaiah the son of Amoz, which he saw concerning Judah and Jerusalem, in the days of Uzziah, Jotham, Ahaz, and Hezekiah, kings of Judah.
Go, and loosen the sackcloth from off your waist, and take your sandals from off your feet.

stages.text: Isaiah son of Amoz: a man in his fifties, lean and sinewy, with a weathered brown skin of the Judean hill country. Dark hair graying at the temples, worn to the shoulders, and a short, full grey beard. Deep-set, steady eyes and a long, lined face marked by years of hard counsel. Signature outfit: a plain undyed linen tunic belted at the waist and a rough brown wool cloak in earth tones. Carries a simple wooden staff, the sign of a traveling prophet.

payload.name: Judah (kingdom and land)
payload.note: The kingdom or land of Judah as a single place across Nehemiah, Isaiah, Joel, Habakkuk and Zephaniah; all entries describe the same territory, distinguished only by the section context in which they appear.

stages.label: Judah

quotes.quote: Woe to those who join house to house, who lay field to field
its gates have been consumed with fire
some of the children of Judah lived in Kiriath Arba and its towns

stages.text: Judah: a hill country of terraced slopes, stony ridges and deep valleys, with walled towns and villages set among olive groves, vineyards and grain fields; Jerusalem on its heights with stone walls, gates and a temple, and fortified citadels; cypress, terebinth and cedar on the uplands.

payload.title: Vision of the new temple's gates

payload.name: Ezekiel son of Buzi
payload.note: Exiled priest and prophet at the river Chebar.

stages.label: Ezekiel son of Buzi

quotes.quote: Yahweh’s word came to Ezekiel the priest, the son of Buzi, in the land of the Chaldeans by the river Chebar

stages.text: Ezekiel son of Buzi: a man of about thirty, lean and steady, with dark hair and a short trimmed beard, bronze-brown skin from desert sun, and a calm, watchful face. He wears a plain undyed linen priestly tunic with a long cloak of rough brown wool over it. He carries a wooden writing tablet and stylus.

payload.name: Man clothed in linen
payload.note: Heavenly figure who marks the faithful with a mark, scatters coals over the city, and measures the new temple with a reed; treated as one guide throughout Ezekiel.

stages.label: Man clothed in linen

quotes.quote: the man clothed in linen, who had the writer’s inkhorn by his side
Take fire from between the whirling wheels, from between the cherubim

stages.text: Man clothed in linen: a figure of mature, steady presence, neither young nor old; lean and upright build; pale bronze skin with a faint radiance; close-cut dark hair and short beard; calm, grave features. Signature outfit: a long white linen tunic and priestly linen sash, plain and unadorned. Carries a scribe's bronze inkhorn at his side and a measuring reed of cane in hand.

payload.name: Ezekiel's temple
payload.note: The Jerusalem temple of Ezekiel's visions of abominations and the measured new temple.

stages.label: Ezekiel's temple

quotes.quote: so that there was the face of a man toward the palm tree on the one side, and the face of a young lion toward the palm tree on the other side.
There were made on them, on the doors of the nave, cherubim and palm trees, like those made on the walls.
He measured the court, one hundred cubits long and one hundred cubits wide, square. The altar was before the house.

stages.text: Ezekiel's temple: a walled sanctuary on the mountain of Jerusalem, built of pale dressed limestone with cedar panelling, its inner court paved and square, its nave carved with cherubim and palm trees between which a face of a man and a face of a young lion alternate. Gates of the outer court face east, north and south; side chambers rise in three stories. Olive and cedar trees line the courts; a river flows from beneath the threshold.

payload.title: Ordeal of jealousy
Against idols and prayer for mercy

payload.name: Jeremiah son of Hilkiah
payload.note: Prophet from Anathoth who speaks most of the book.

stages.label: Jeremiah

quotes.quote: The words of Jeremiah the son of Hilkiah, one of the priests who were in Anathoth in the land of Benjamin.
They let down Jeremiah with cords. In the dungeon there was no water, but mire; and Jeremiah sank in the mire.

stages.text: Jeremiah: a man in his middle years, lean and weathered from long journeys and imprisonment, with a grave, careworn face and deep-set dark eyes. Close-cropped dark hair and a short greying beard. Dark-skinned Levantine complexion. Wears a plain undyed linen priestly tunic under a long brown wool cloak, the cloak worn thin at the hem. Carries a plain wooden staff.

payload.title: Gideon's three hundred and the rout of Midian

payload.name: Gideon
payload.note: Manassite judge called by Yahweh's angel, also called Jerubbaal and son of Joash.

stages.label: Gideon

quotes.quote: His son Gideon was beating out wheat in the wine press
you mighty man of valor!

stages.text: Gideon: a man in his thirties, of lean, sturdy build with weathered brown skin from threshing and field labour. Dark brown hair falls to his shoulders, with a short trimmed beard. Steady, deep-set eyes and a broad, serious face. He wears a plain undyed woven linen tunic belted at the waist under a rust-brown wool cloak. Carries a simple wooden threshing staff or a plain sword.

payload.name: Purah
payload.note: Servant who goes with Gideon into the Midianite camp at night.

stages.label: Purah

quotes.quote: go with Purah your servant down to the camp
Then went he down with Purah his servant to the outermost part of the armed men

stages.text: Purah: a young man in his twenties, lean and wiry, of middle stature. Olive-brown skin weathered by desert sun. Dark hair cropped close, a short trimmed beard. Steady, attentive eyes and a calm, open face. He wears a plain woven wool tunic in undyed brown with a dark blue cloak, and carries a leather water skin across his shoulder.

aliases: the God of our Lord Jesus Christ
him who sits on the throne
payload.name: God / Yahweh, the Father and God of Israel
payload.note: The one God, creator and speaker of the Old Testament and the Father of Jesus Christ in the New Testament; distinct from Jesus in every entry.

stages.label: God the Father (radiance and cloud)

quotes.quote: Heaven is my throne, and the earth is my footstool.
Behold, Yahweh rides on a swift cloud, and comes to Egypt.

stages.text: God the Father: no human face or body; presence shown only as radiance, cloud and fire. A brilliant white-gold light without a source, veiled by a dense, slowly moving cloud, with a fire-like glow at its heart. Throne-light and footstool-earth implied at the edges, never a figure seated in it.

payload.name: Tribe of Ephraim (men of Ephraim)
payload.note: The Israelite tribe in the judges' era that quarrels with Gideon and Jephthah; distinct from the person and from the northern kingdom.

stages.label: Men of Ephraim

quotes.quote: The men of Ephraim were gathered together, and passed northward
At that time, forty-two thousand of Ephraim fell.

stages.text: Men of Ephraim: adult men, late twenties to forties; sturdy, weathered build; olive-brown skin; dark hair worn to the shoulder and short, close-trimmed beards; strong brows and steady eyes. Signature dress: a dark-blue woven wool tunic belted at the waist under a rust-brown cloak. Carry a round leather shield and a short spear.

payload.name: Midianites of Judges
payload.note: Raiding peoples in Judges who oppress Israel for seven years and are defeated by Gideon's three hundred; distinguished by the Gideon context and the Zebah and Zalmunna pursuit.

stages.label: Midianites of Judges

quotes.quote: Yahweh delivered them into the hand of Midian seven years.
lay along in the valley like locusts for multitude; and their camels were without number

stages.text: Midianites of Judges: adult men, ages twenty to forty; lean, weathered desert build; olive-bronze skin; dark hair bound back with a cord, short beards; hard, watchful faces. Signature outfit: a long undyed wool robe in ochre and dun, belted at the waist, with a dark-brown cloak against the wind. Signature props: a curved sword and a leather sling at the belt.

payload.name: spring of Harod
payload.note: Where Gideon encamps and tests his men by drinking water.

stages.label: Spring of Harod

quotes.quote: encamped beside the spring of Harod
by the hill of Moreh, in the valley

stages.text: Spring of Harod: a clear, cold spring rising at the foot of a rocky slope in the broad valley of Jezreel, its water collecting in a shallow pool edged with smooth stones. Tamarisk and wild reeds grow along the margin, with grey-green scrub and terebinth on the higher ground. Beyond the water rises the low hill of Moreh to the north, its flanks bare stone and thin grass, the valley floor stretching open and dusty.

payload.name: Midian's camp (Valley of Jezreel)
payload.note: Valley where Gideon routs the Midianite host; also called the valley of Jezreel in aliases, so it may be one of the Jezreel places but is a different valley from Hosea's Jezreel.

stages.label: Midian's camp, valley of Jezreel

quotes.quote: they passed over, and encamped in the valley of Jezreel.

stages.text: Midian's camp, valley of Jezreel: a broad, open lowland of dry grass and scattered thornbush, ringed by low hills. Black goat-hair tents are pitched in wide rows across the flat ground, with cooking hearths and stacked camels' saddles between them. Stone-walled wells and a few clay-walled threshing floors mark the edges, and tall terebinth trees stand along the watercourse.

payload.name: Mount Gilead (Gideon's base)
payload.note: The mountain in Judges from which Gideon sends home the fearful before the rout of Midian; not the Genesis covenant site.

stages.label: Mount Gilead (Gideon's base)

quotes.quote: let him return and depart from Mount Gilead

stages.text: Mount Gilead: a broad, rolling highland east of the Jordan, its slopes of grey limestone scattered with terebinth and oak, wild grasses and thorn scrub. Terraced hillsides hold low stone walls and dry-stone field boundaries. A spring runs from rock at the foot of the ridge, with a shallow pool beside a worn track. Few built structures; watch-cairns and a cluster of tents mark the camp.

payload.title: Laws of war, homicide and everyday justice

payload.name: Moses
payload.note: Israel's lawgiver and leader who led the people out of Egypt, received the law at Sinai and is named across the Old and New Testament divisions as the same individual, distinguished only by the sections in which he appears or is mentioned.

stages.label: Moses, elder

quotes.quote: Moses was eighty years old, and Aaron eighty-three years old, when they spoke to Pharaoh.

stages.text: Moses: an old man of about eighty; lean, weathered build; brown skin darkened by desert sun; white hair and a long white beard; deep-set, steady eyes and lined brow; a plain undyed linen tunic belted at the waist with a long dark-brown wool cloak; he carries a wooden shepherd's staff of dark acacia wood, and only he bears the rod of God.

stages.label: Moses, infant

quotes.quote: The woman conceived and bore a son. When she saw that he was a fine child, she hid him three months.

stages.text: Moses: a newborn infant; soft smooth skin; a small round face; a little dark hair; wrapped in plain linen cloth and laid in a woven reed basket sealed with bitumen and pitch; no beard, no staff, no adult clothing.

stages.label: Moses, adult

quotes.quote: But when he was forty years old, it came into his heart to visit his brothers, the children of Israel.

stages.text: Moses: a man of about forty; lean, strong, well-proportioned build; brown skin; short dark hair and a close-trimmed dark beard; alert, sober face; a knee-length undyed linen tunic with a dark woven wool cloak of brown and grey pinned at the shoulder; he carries a plain wooden shepherd's staff.

aliases: those who came out of Egypt
payload.name: The Israelite people (the children of Israel)
payload.note: The collective Israelite nation across Exodus through Malachi and Hebrews, one body whose different portrayals (marching nation, assembly, covenant people, judged northern kingdom, returned community, wilderness generation) are all the same people; distinguish only from the returned community of Nehemiah in the note by the Judah/Jerusalem setting, but these are the same people.

stages.label: The Israelite people

quotes.quote: Now these are the names of the sons of Israel, who came into Egypt
You shall tell the children of Israel this
So they shall put my name on the children of Israel; and I will bless them.

stages.text: The Israelite people: a typical member is an adult of mixed age, from youth to middle years, of sturdy and weathered build shaped by desert travel and field labour. Skin is warm olive-brown, hair dark and kept short or tied back, with full beards on men. Faces are calm and steady with dark eyes. Signature outfit: a plain undyed woven linen tunic in ochre or cream with a wool cloak in earth brown.

aliases: the priests who bear the ark
payload.name: The priests and Levites (Deuteronomy)
payload.note: The Levitical priests who bear the ark and minister and judge in Deuteronomy's ritual and legal scenes.

stages.label: The priests and Levites

quotes.quote: the priests the sons of Levi, who bore the ark of Yahweh’s covenant
You shall command the priests who bear the ark of the covenant

stages.text: The priests and Levites: adult men of middle age, sturdy and dignified; olive-brown skin of the Levant; close-cropped dark hair and a short trimmed beard; calm, grave features. Signature outfit: a white woven linen tunic and sash with a blue-violet priestly robe and cloak, plain and clean. Carry the ark's poles on the shoulder.

payload.name: Elders, judges and officers of Deuteronomy
payload.note: Tribal judges and officers who hear cases and receive the law in Deuteronomy.

stages.label: Elders, judges and officers of Deuteronomy

quotes.quote: then both the men, between whom the controversy is, shall stand before Yahweh, before the priests and the judges
then his father and his mother shall take hold of him and bring him out to the elders of his city and to the gate of his place.

stages.text: Elders, judges and officers: men of middle to advanced age, mostly weathered and grey-bearded; sturdy build; olive-brown skin; short grey-streaked beards and close-cropped hair; calm, serious faces. Signature outfit: a long woven undertunic of undyed linen under a deep indigo cloak with a plain woven border. Carry a short wooden staff of office.

aliases: the hill country of the Amorites
payload.name: Canaan
payload.note: The promised land of Israel as a whole, the land Yahweh gives to Abram's descendants, referred to in Genesis, Leviticus, Numbers, Deuteronomy, Judges and Hebrews alike; all six entries describe this same land.

stages.label: Canaan, the promised land

quotes.quote: Surely it flows with milk and honey, and this is its fruit.
Behold, Yahweh your God has set the land before you.
to the Western Sea
the land where you are traveling, all the land of Canaan, for an everlasting possession
seven nations greater and mightier than you

stages.text: Canaan: a fertile hill country between the Jordan river and the Western Sea, with terraced slopes, olive groves, vineyards heavy with grapes, wheat fields in the valleys, and wells beside walled mud-brick and stone towns on the hilltops. Scattered oaks and terebinths mark old sacred places, and herders' pastures roll toward the distant coast.

payload.title: David's letter and Uriah's death

aliases: the anointed of the God of Jacob
payload.name: David son of Jesse (king of Israel)
payload.note: The single David of the Hebrew books and the New Testament references: son of Jesse, shepherd, harpist, anointed king, father of Solomon; all entries describe this one king and the hint's second David is not needed.

stages.label: David as king

quotes.quote: David was thirty years old when he began to reign, and he reigned forty years.

stages.text: David: a man of about thirty to fifty, athletic and broad-shouldered, of medium height; ruddy complexion, bright dark eyes, short dark beard trimmed close; dark hair cut to the shoulder. Signature outfit: a long blue royal robe with a sash of crimson and gold, over an undertunic of white linen. Carries a bronze-bossed sword in a leather scabbard and a harp.

stages.label: David as youth

quotes.quote: He sent, and brought him in. Now he was ruddy, with a handsome face and good appearance. Yahweh said, “Arise! Anoint him, for this is he.”

stages.text: David: a beardless youth and young adult before kingship; slender, wiry build, ruddy complexion, bright dark eyes and short dark curly hair. Plain undyed brown wool tunic, leather belt and sandals; shepherd's pouch and sling when called for. No crown or royal robes.

stages.label: David as elder

quotes.quote: Now King David was old and advanced in years; and they covered him with clothes, but he couldn’t keep warm.

stages.text: David: an old man of about seventy, lean and bent with age, his frame still dignified; ruddy complexion faded to a weathered warmth, dark eyes deep-set and gentle, white hair and a white beard cut short. Signature outfit: a plain long wool robe of undyed cream with a dark blue cloak over the shoulders for warmth. Carries a staff of almond wood.

payload.name: Joab
payload.note: Son of Zeruiah and David's army commander, who kills Abner, Absalom and Amasa and leads the Ammonite campaign; distinguish from other Joabs by his role as David's commander in the army.

stages.label: Joab, captain of David's army

quotes.quote: Joab was clothed in his apparel of war that he had put on, and on it was a sash with a sword fastened on his waist in its sheath
He took three darts in his hand and thrust them through Absalom’s heart
Ten young men who bore Joab’s armor surrounded and struck Absalom

stages.text: Joab: a man in his middle years, around forty to fifty, of strong, weathered build with broad shoulders and a soldier's stance. Skin olive-brown and sun-browned. Dark hair cropped short at the neck, with a close-trimmed beard streaked with grey at the chin. Hard, watchful face with a broken nose. Signature outfit: a bronze-scaled or leather-plated military coat over a dark undertunic, with a deep red-brown war sash at the waist. Carries a sword in a plain sheath and three darts in hand.

payload.name: David's royal palace in Jerusalem
payload.note: The king's house in Jerusalem where David's scenes unfold (Bathsheba, Uriah, Nathan, Amnon and Tamar); distinguish from the other royal houses by its Davidic setting.

stages.label: David's royal palace in Jerusalem

quotes.quote: went up to the room over the gate and wept

stages.text: David's royal palace in Jerusalem: a substantial citadel of dressed ashlar stone and cedar-beamed timber, set on the ridge of the City of David above the Kidron valley. Flat-roofed stone halls rise in terraces, with a gate tower of heavy masonry whose upper chamber, the room over the gate, has latticed windows. Olive trees and terraced vineyards grow on the slopes below; cypress and terebinth stand near the walls.

aliases: Rabbah of the children of Ammon
land of the children of Ammon
payload.name: Rabbah (Ammonite capital)
payload.note: The Ammonite capital city, Rabbah, besieged by Joab and taken by David in 2 Samuel and 1 Chronicles, and judged in Amos; the same city across all three books.

stages.label: Rabbah, Ammonite capital

quotes.quote: Joab fought against Rabbah of the children of Ammon, and took the royal city.
I have fought against Rabbah. Yes, I have taken the city of waters.
I will kindle a fire in the wall of Rabbah, and it will devour its palaces
made them go to the brick kiln

stages.text: Rabbah: a fortified highland city of the Ammonites set in a river valley of the Transjordan, with thick mudbrick and fieldstone walls and a massive gate tower of stone. Within its walls rise stone-built palaces with cedar beams and terraced rooftops, and a citadel on the high ground. Terraced fields, olive and fig trees, and a dark-green stream of water run through the valley below the walls. Brick kilns stand outside the city.

payload.title: Wisdom's creative role and everyday counsel

payload.name: Solomon
payload.note: Son of David and Bathsheba, king of Israel who builds the temple; the same individual across all divisions. Distinguish from the Shulammite's shepherd beloved, who is not Solomon.

stages.label: Solomon, king of Israel

quotes.quote: had Solomon ride on King David’s mule, and brought him to Gihon.
sat down on his throne and caused a throne to be set for the king’s mother

stages.text: Solomon: man in his twenties to forties, lean and upright with a composed, dignified bearing; warm olive-brown skin; dark curly hair and a short, neatly trimmed beard; calm, thoughtful face with a broad brow. Signature outfit: a long deep-blue royal court robe with gold-thread borders over a white linen tunic, and a gold circlet on his head. Signature prop: a plain rod of royal authority carried alone.

payload.title: Ahaz's Damascus altar

aliases: king of Judah son of Jotham
payload.name: Ahaz
payload.note: King of Judah son of Jotham who calls on Assyria.

stages.label: Ahaz, king of Judah

quotes.quote: Ahaz was twenty years old when he began to reign, and he reigned sixteen years in Jerusalem.
Ahaz the son of Jotham king of Judah began to reign.

stages.text: Ahaz: man in his twenties to late thirties, lean and upright; olive-toned skin weathered by sun; short dark beard trimmed close, dark hair bound back under a simple gold-banded headcloth; drawn, anxious face with heavy brows and a set mouth. Signature outfit: a long purple-edged court robe over a linen tunic, in deep blue and madder red, with a leather belt. Carries alone a bronze-bound royal staff of dark wood.

payload.name: Urijah the priest
payload.note: Priest who builds an altar in the Damascus style at Ahaz's order.

stages.label: Urijah the priest

quotes.quote: Urijah the priest built an altar.
King Ahaz sent to Urijah the priest a drawing of the altar

stages.text: Urijah the priest: a man in middle age, lean and steady in build, olive-brown skin, close-cropped dark hair and a short trimmed beard threaded with grey, lines of care about the eyes and mouth. Signature outfit: a plain white priestly linen tunic belted with a blue-violet sash, over it a short linen ephod in undyed cream. Carries no props alone.

payload.name: Damascus
payload.note: Capital city of Syria, seat of Ben-hadad and Rezon, and home of Naaman's rivers, judged in Amos and linked with Paul's conversion and escape in Acts and 2 Corinthians; all entries here are the same city.

stages.label: Damascus

quotes.quote: synagogues of Damascus
the rivers of Damascus
guarded the Damascenes’ city
went up against Damascus and took it

stages.text: Damascus: a walled oasis city of pale limestone and mud-brick houses with flat roofs and domes, set against arid hills; date palms, orchards and irrigated gardens watered by the rivers Abanah and Pharpar; a city gate with a wall, and a straight main street lined with walls and shaded arcades.

aliases: the house which is called by my name
the tent of the daughter of Zion
the house of Yahweh of Armies
payload.name: Yahweh's house in Jerusalem (the temple)
payload.note: The one Jerusalem temple (Yahweh's house, the sanctuary on Mount Moriah) across all references, from Solomon's building through repair, destruction and rebuilding; construction and ruin are later appearance stages, not separate places.

stages.label: Solomon's temple on Mount Moriah

quotes.quote: The house, when it was under construction, was built of stone prepared at the quarry
Within the inner sanctuary was twenty cubits in length, and twenty cubits in width, and twenty cubits in its height.
He overlaid the floor of the house with gold, inside and outside.
Also he made before the house two pillars thirty-five cubits high
He set the sea on the right side of the house eastward and toward the south.

stages.text: Yahweh's house in Jerusalem: a stone temple of finished ashlar on Mount Moriah, roofed with cedar beams, its inner sanctuary panelled in cedar and overlaid with pure gold. Carved cherubim, palm and open flowers cover the doors and walls. Before the house stand two great bronze pillars and a huge bronze molten sea on twelve oxen. Courts of stone surround it, with olive and cypress trees, and the walled city of Jerusalem rises beyond.

payload.title: Song of Deborah and Barak

payload.name: Deborah
payload.note: Prophetess and judge of Israel under her palm tree, wife of Lappidoth, who sends for Barak and sings the song of chapter 5; distinct from the other prophetesses in this group.

stages.label: Deborah, prophetess and judge

quotes.quote: Now Deborah, a prophetess, the wife of Lappidoth, judged Israel at that time.
She lived under Deborah’s palm tree between Ramah and Bethel in the hill country of Ephraim
Until I arose a mother in Israel.

stages.text: Deborah: woman of mature years, perhaps fifties, upright and steady; medium build; warm brown skin of the hill country; dark hair worn covered beneath a linen headcloth edged in blue; calm, dignified face with deep-set dark eyes and a firm mouth. Signature outfit: a long undyed linen tunic under a deep ochre woven cloak with a blue border. Signature prop: a slender palm-wood staff of judgment carried alone.

payload.name: Barak
payload.note: Naphtali commander who fights Sisera at Mount Tabor.

stages.label: Barak

quotes.quote: She sent and called Barak the son of Abinoam out of Kedesh Naphtali
Barak called Zebulun and Naphtali together to Kedesh.

stages.text: Barak: man in his prime, roughly thirty to forty years old; sturdy, broad-shouldered, weathered build from war and hill country; olive-brown skin; dark hair worn to the shoulder and a short, close-trimmed dark beard; steady, resolute face with a strong brow. Signature outfit: a woven undyed wool tunic with a long dark-red wool cloak fastened at the shoulder. Carries no props alone.

payload.name: Jael
payload.note: Wife of Heber the Kenite who kills Sisera with a tent peg in her tent; the only Jael in these divisions.

stages.label: Jael

quotes.quote: the tent of Jael the wife of Heber the Kenite
Jael, Heber’s wife, took a tent peg, and took a hammer in her hand
Jael shall be blessed above women, the wife of Heber the Kenite

stages.text: Jael: a woman of about thirty-five to forty, sturdy and steady in build, with warm olive-brown skin weathered by desert sun. Dark hair is bound up and covered by a plain linen head cloth. Her face is calm, strong and grave. Her signature outfit, worn most often, is a long undyed woven wool tunic in deep indigo with a rust-red woven cloak. She carries a heavy iron tent peg and a hammer as her own tools.

aliases: the mother looking through the lattice
payload.name: Sisera's mother
payload.note: Mother of Sisera who waits for his return in the song of chapter 5; distinct from Sisera himself.

stages.label: Sisera's mother

quotes.quote: Her wise ladies answered her, Yes, she returned answer to herself,

stages.text: Sisera's mother: a woman of middle to later years, slender and upright, with warm olive-brown skin and fine lines at her eyes. Her dark hair is bound under a woven linen headcloth, and a few grey strands show at the temples. Her face is grave and composed. Her signature outfit is a long undyed linen tunic under a deep indigo wool cloak with a woven band at the hem. She carries a small carved wooden lattice-frame window screen beside her, and a fine linen veil hangs from her shoulders.

payload.name: river Kishon
payload.note: Riverside battlefield where Sisera's chariots are swept away.

stages.label: River Kishon

quotes.quote: to the river Kishon, Sisera, the captain of Jabin’s army, with his chariots and his multitude
The river Kishon swept them away, that ancient river, the river Kishon.

stages.text: River Kishon: a broad, ancient, slow-moving river across the fertile plain of Jezreel, its banks lined with reeds, tamarisk and oleander, with low clay banks, muddy fords and soft silt that can swallow wheels. Low rounded hills rise in the distance, and the walled Canaanite towns of the plain stand on the heights beyond the water.

payload.name: Mount Tabor
payload.note: Where Barak musters his men against Sisera in Judges.

stages.label: Mount Tabor

quotes.quote: Go and lead the way to Mount Tabor, and take with you ten thousand men
So Barak went down from Mount Tabor, and ten thousand men after him.

stages.text: Mount Tabor: a solitary, dome-shaped mountain rising abruptly from the broad plain of Jezreel in northern Israel; its slopes are rounded and grassed with terebinth and oak scattered among limestone outcrops; the summit is a flat, rocky crown; no buildings are visible on its open ridges, only low stone walls and ancient terraces; earth in ochre and olive tones.

payload.title: Isaiah's vision of Yahweh in the temple

payload.name: Isaiah son of Amoz
payload.note: Prophet who advises Hezekiah; the same prophet across Isaiah, 2 Kings and 2 Chronicles.

stages.label: Isaiah son of Amoz

quotes.quote: The vision of Isaiah the son of Amoz, which he saw concerning Judah and Jerusalem, in the days of Uzziah, Jotham, Ahaz, and Hezekiah, kings of Judah.
Go, and loosen the sackcloth from off your waist, and take your sandals from off your feet.

stages.text: Isaiah son of Amoz: a man in his fifties, lean and sinewy, with a weathered brown skin of the Judean hill country. Dark hair graying at the temples, worn to the shoulders, and a short, full grey beard. Deep-set, steady eyes and a long, lined face marked by years of hard counsel. Signature outfit: a plain undyed linen tunic belted at the waist and a rough brown wool cloak in earth tones. Carries a simple wooden staff, the sign of a traveling prophet.

payload.name: Seraphim
payload.note: Six-winged beings around the throne in Isaiah 6 who call out and touch Isaiah's lips with a coal; a class of heavenly beings, not a single individual.

stages.label: Seraphim

quotes.quote: Each one had six wings. With two he covered his face. With two he covered his feet. With two he flew.
one of the seraphim flew to me, having a live coal in his hand, which he had taken with the tongs from off the altar.

stages.text: Seraphim: a heavenly being of tall, luminous human-like form, ageless, with burnished bronze-gold skin. Six wings: two cover the face, two cover the feet, two lift in flight, feathered in white and gold. Face hidden behind the wings. Robed in a long linen tunic of pale white. Carries a glowing live coal held in long iron tongs, the coal burning orange-red.

payload.title: Job's despair in the grave

payload.name: Job
payload.note: Blameless, wealthy man of Uz who loses his family and health and debates with his friends and with Yahweh.

stages.label: Job

quotes.quote: There was a man in the land of Uz, whose name was Job. That man was blameless and upright, and one who feared God, and turned away from evil.
Then Job arose, and tore his robe, and shaved his head, and fell down on the ground, and worshiped.
So Satan went out from the presence of Yahweh, and struck Job with painful sores from the sole of his foot to his head.

stages.text: Job: man of middle to later years, perhaps fifty to sixty, of sturdy but weathered build; dark brown skin; short, graying hair with a close-trimmed beard shaved at the head in grief; dignified, lined face with deep-set eyes. Signature outfit: a long undyed linen tunic with a deep indigo wool cloak over it. Carries a shepherd's staff of olive wood. Sores on skin in later sections.

payload.name: The ash heap
payload.note: Place outside the city where Job sits, scraping his sores with a potsherd (2:8).

stages.label: The ash heap

quotes.quote: He took for himself a potsherd to scrape himself with, and he sat among the ashes.
houses of clay, whose foundation is in the dust

stages.text: The ash heap: a broad low mound of grey and white ash, dust and broken clay outside the city walls, sloping gently to bare dry ground. Scattered potsherds, cracked jars and cinders lie in drifts; sparse scrub and thorn bushes grow at its edges. Distant city walls, gates and roofs of sun-baked brick rise on the horizon.

payload.title: Proverbs on the city, the righteous and the wicked
Inheritances of the remaining tribes

payload.name: Joshua son of Nun
payload.note: Son of Nun of Ephraim, Moses' aide and successor who leads Israel into Canaan; the same individual across Exodus, Numbers, Deuteronomy, Joshua, Judges (as the deceased) and Hebrews, so no other Joshua is separated from him in this group.

stages.label: Joshua son of Nun

quotes.quote: Joshua defeated Amalek and his people with the edge of the sword.
his servant Joshua, the son of Nun, a young man, didn’t depart from the Tent.
Joshua was old and well advanced in years

stages.text: Joshua son of Nun: a man of mature strength in his prime, aged about forty to fifty when leading, with a sturdy, broad-shouldered build and weathered brown skin marked by desert sun. Short dark hair, close-cropped beard, steady deep-set eyes and a firm, grave face. Signature outfit: a plain undyed linen tunic and a dark brown woven wool cloak. Carries a bronze-bladed sword at his belt and a long wooden spear.

aliases: the sons of Aaron who were left
payload.name: Eleazar son of Aaron
payload.note: Third son of Aaron, later priest who oversees Levite duties and succeeds Aaron.

stages.label: Eleazar, priest

quotes.quote: that they make Aaron’s garments to sanctify him, that he may minister to me in the priest’s office.
Eleazar and Ithamar ministered in the priest’s office in the presence of Aaron their father.

stages.text: Eleazar: a man in his middle years, sturdy and dignified; olive-brown skin weathered by desert sun; short dark beard streaked with early grey; a calm, grave face with deep-set eyes. His signature outfit is a white linen priestly tunic with a blue-violet woven robe and a fine embroidered sash, a linen turban. He carries a bronze censer or a priest's staff.

aliases: the house of Yahweh at Shiloh
payload.name: Shiloh
payload.note: The sanctuary town where the Tent of Meeting stands and lots are cast in Joshua, the feast site where Benjamin's men seize wives in Judges, the house of Yahweh where the ark stood with Eli and Samuel in 1 Samuel, and the old sanctuary where Ahijah lives in 1 Kings; all four entries are the same place across the books.

stages.label: Shiloh

quotes.quote: set up the Tent of Meeting there
sitting on his seat by the doorpost of Yahweh’s temple
on the east side of the highway that goes up from Bethel to Shechem
come out of the vineyards

stages.text: Shiloh: a hill town in the central highlands of Canaan on a rise above a valley, with terraced limestone slopes, olive groves and vineyards on the surrounding hills. At its centre stands a plain sanctuary of pale stone and timber, its open doorway flanked by wooden doorposts, a tent-like enclosure of woven cloth and goatskin within a courtyard wall. A highway runs past the town toward Bethel and Shechem.

payload.title: The assembly and the covenant to put away foreign wives

payload.name: Ezra the priest and scribe
payload.note: Priest and scribe, son of Seraiah, who leads the return from Babylon and calls for the putting away of foreign wives.

stages.label: Ezra the priest and scribe

quotes.quote: He was a skilled scribe in the law of Moses, which Yahweh, the God of Israel, had given
Now while Ezra prayed and made confession, weeping and casting himself down before God’s house

stages.text: Ezra the priest and scribe: a man in his middle years, lean and upright, with dark-grey-streaked brown hair and a short trimmed beard. Olive-brown skin, deep-set serious eyes, lined brow. Signature outfit: a plain undyed linen priestly tunic and white linen mitre-cap with a dark-blue woven sash, over which a long undyed wool cloak. Carries a rolled scroll of the law in a leather case.

payload.name: Shecaniah
payload.note: Man of Elam who speaks to Ezra and proposes the covenant to put away foreign wives.

stages.label: Shecaniah son of Jehiel

quotes.quote: Shecaniah the son of Jehiel, one of the sons of Elam, answered Ezra

stages.text: Shecaniah: a man in his forties, of middling height and sturdy build from years of returned-exile labour. Skin warm olive-brown; short dark hair under a plain cloth head covering, with a close-trimmed beard streaked with early grey. Lined, grave face with steady dark eyes. Signature outfit: a long undyed linen tunic and a deep rust-red wool cloak fastened at the shoulder. Carries no props.

payload.name: People of Judah and Benjamin (Ezra)
payload.note: The returned exiles gathered in Jerusalem who act together in the assembly in Ezra.

stages.label: People of Judah and Benjamin

quotes.quote: and all Israel in their cities.
The children of Israel, the priests, the Levites, and the rest of the children of the captivity

stages.text: People of Judah and Benjamin: a typical member is an adult Israelite man or woman of working age, between about 25 and 55, of sturdy, weathered build from farm and building labour. Skin olive-brown, hair dark and often covered by a head cloth; men bearded, short beards kept trimmed. Faces lined, serious and dignified. Signature outfit: a plain undyed linen tunic with a long brown or indigo wool cloak; sandals. Props carried alone: a simple clay water jar or a builder's tool.

payload.name: Jonathan son of Asahel
payload.note: Man who stood with Jahzeiah against the plan to put away foreign wives in Ezra's time. Distinguished by his father Asahel and his role in the assembly.

stages.label: Jonathan son of Asahel

quotes.quote: Only Jonathan the son of Asahel and Jahzeiah the son of Tikvah stood up against this

stages.text: Jonathan son of Asahel: middle-aged man, around fifty; sturdy build; olive-brown skin; short dark beard streaked with grey; lined, steady face with a serious brow; wears a plain undyed wool tunic and a dark brown cloak over the shoulders; carries a simple wooden staff of an elder.

payload.name: Meshullam the Levite (Ezra)
payload.note: Levite in Ezra's assembly who helps Jonathan and Jahzeiah oppose the separation from foreign wives; distinct from other Meshullams by this context.

stages.label: Meshullam the Levite

quotes.quote: and for Meshullam, chief men
Meshullam and Shabbethai the Levite helped them.

stages.text: Meshullam the Levite: man in his middle years, around forty to fifty; sturdy, unhurried build; olive-brown skin; short dark beard streaked with grey and close-cropped dark hair; grave, steady face with deep-set eyes. Signature outfit: a plain undyed linen tunic with a dark indigo wool cloak. Carries no props of his own.

payload.name: Shabbethai the Levite
payload.note: Levite who opposes the separation from foreign wives alongside Jonathan and Meshullam in Ezra; a different individual from Meshullam.

stages.label: Shabbethai the Levite

quotes.quote: Meshullam and Shabbethai the Levite helped them.

stages.text: Shabbethai the Levite: man in his middle years, lean and steady of build, olive-brown skin, close-cut dark hair and a short trimmed beard greying at the chin, lined brow and calm, sober eyes. Wears a plain white linen tunic belted with a woven band in blue and red, over it a dark undyed wool cloak. Carries a worn leather scroll case slung at the hip.

payload.name: Jehohanan
payload.note: Man in whose room Ezra mourns; the room belongs to him.

stages.label: Jehohanan, son of Eliashib

quotes.quote: went into the room of Jehohanan the son of Eliashib
Of the sons of Bebai: Jehohanan, Hananiah, Zabbai, and Athlai.

stages.text: Jehohanan: a man in middle age, sturdy and dignified; olive skin, dark hair and a short trimmed beard greying at the chin; calm, steady face with deep-set eyes. His signature outfit is a plain undyed linen tunic with a woollen cloak of deep blue-brown and a white head cloth. No props.

aliases: the city of my fathers' tombs
payload.name: Jerusalem
payload.note: The capital city of Judah (also called Jebus, David's city, the holy city, Zion as city in some books); the city itself, distinct from the hill/mountain of Zion as a place of Yahweh's dwelling.

stages.label: Jerusalem

quotes.quote: they buried him in David's city
a breach was made in the city

stages.text: Jerusalem: a walled city on a steep limestone ridge of the Judean hills, terraces of olive and fig trees falling into deep valleys. Stone and mud-brick houses with flat roofs crowd the slopes; a fortified citadel of the stronghold of Zion stands on the high ground. Massive city walls with gates, and above the city the temple mount crowned by a stone-built temple of Yahweh.

payload.title: Genealogy from Adam to the kings of Edom
Gedaliah's governorship and murder

payload.name: Gedaliah son of Ahikam
payload.note: Babylon-appointed governor of Judah at Mizpah, son of Ahikam, assassinated by Ishmael; the same individual as in the Jeremiah account, so both entries join this cluster.

stages.label: Gedaliah son of Ahikam

quotes.quote: even over them he made Gedaliah the son of Ahikam, the son of Shaphan, governor.

stages.text: Gedaliah son of Ahikam: man in his forties; lean, upright build; olive-brown skin; short dark beard, neatly trimmed; hair cropped to the nape; calm, grave face. Signature outfit: a long undyed linen tunic under a dark blue court cloak with a plain woven band at the hem, showing his office. Carries no props.

payload.name: Ishmael son of Nethaniah
payload.note: Royal assassin who murders governor Gedaliah at Mizpah (2 Kings 25, Jeremiah 40-41); identified by his father Nethaniah and the Gedaliah murder.

stages.label: Ishmael son of Nethaniah

quotes.quote: Ishmael the son of Nethaniah, the son of Elishama, of the royal offspring and one of the chief officers of the king

stages.text: Ishmael son of Nethaniah: a man of about forty, lean and upright, of royal Judahite lineage. Dark hair cropped close to the head and a short dark beard, face weathered and watchful. Wears a plain undyed linen tunic under a dark brown wool cloak with a court officer's band of deep red at the hem. Carries a bronze-bladed sword at his hip alone.

payload.name: Mizpah (Judean town of Gedaliah's murder)
payload.note: The Judean town in 2 Kings and Jeremiah where Gedaliah governs and is murdered by Ishmael; the 2 Kings and Jeremiah entries describe the same place and are joined on that basis.

stages.label: Mizpah

quotes.quote: all the Jews returned out of all places where they were driven, and came to the land of Judah, to Gedaliah, to Mizpah, and gathered very much wine and summer fruits.
dwell in your cities that you have taken.

stages.text: Mizpah: a hilltop town of Judah on a ridge above open valleys, its low stone houses of rough-hewn limestone with flat roofs and mud-plaster, a fortified city wall with a gate of heavy timber and stone, a central open space near the gate, scattered olive trees, terraced vineyards and fig trees on the slopes, and a watchtower on the highest point.

payload.title: Yahweh is my portion
Letter to Philadelphia

aliases: the apostle and high priest of our confession
the great shepherd of the sheep
the author and perfecter of faith
the mediator of a new covenant
the Lion of the tribe of Judah
the rider called Faithful and True
KING OF KINGS AND LORD OF LORDS
payload.name: Jesus Christ, the Son of God and Lord
payload.note: The one Jesus: the teacher from Nazareth of the Gospels and Acts, and the risen, exalted Christ and Lord of the epistles and Revelation; the same individual across all divisions, with death, resurrection and changed portrayal not creating new individuals.

stages.label: Adult Jesus

quotes.quote: Jesus himself, when he began to teach, was about thirty years old, being the son (as was supposed) of Joseph, the son of Heli,

stages.text: Jesus: man of about thirty, lean and strong from carpentry and walking; olive-brown skin; dark brown shoulder-length hair parted at centre; short dark beard; calm dark eyes; wears a plain undyed tunic of natural linen with a dark blue-grey cloak and sandals; carries no props except a shepherd's staff when a scene calls for one.

stages.label: Infant Jesus

quotes.quote: She gave birth to her firstborn son. She wrapped him in bands of cloth and laid him in a feeding trough, because there was no room for them in the inn.

stages.text: Jesus: newborn to about two years old; olive-brown skin, a little dark hair and dark eyes; a small infant or toddler's build, no beard. Plain undyed swaddling linen for the newborn; a small plain linen tunic as a toddler. No adult clothing or props.

stages.label: Boy Jesus

quotes.quote: When he was twelve years old, they went up to Jerusalem according to the custom of the feast;

stages.text: Jesus: boy of about twelve, slim and sturdy; olive-brown skin; dark brown hair cut short at the neck; dark eyes; no beard; wears a plain undyed tunic of natural linen with a dark blue-grey cloak; no props.

payload.name: the seven churches of Asia
payload.note: A collective place name for the seven assemblies in Asia addressed in Revelation 2 and 3, of which Ephesus is one; distinct from the single city of Ephesus.

stages.label: The seven churches of Asia

quotes.quote: send to the seven assemblies: to Ephesus, Smyrna, Pergamum, Thyatira, Sardis, Philadelphia, and to Laodicea.

stages.text: The seven churches of Asia: a scatter of coastal and inland cities across western Anatolia, joined by old Roman roads. Whitewashed stone houses, marble colonnades, and tiled roofs rise on terraced hills above river valleys. Olive groves, vines and cypresses grow along the slopes, and distant mountains rise blue and rocky beyond.

payload.title: Wish for a brother and the adjuration

payload.name: The Shulammite
payload.note: The dark but lovely bride of the Song of Solomon who speaks most of the Song; keeper of her brothers' vineyards. Distinct from the figurative bride of Revelation.

stages.label: The Shulammite

quotes.quote: Your eyes are like doves behind your veil. Your hair is as a flock of goats, that descend from Mount Gilead.
with one chain of your neck.

stages.text: The Shulammite: a young woman of about eighteen to twenty; slender, graceful build; warm dark skin tanned by sun from working the vineyards; long dark hair, thick and flowing like goats descending Gilead, often partly veiled; large dove-like dark eyes, soft gaze, full lips, a fine chain at her neck; signature outfit a plain undyed linen tunic with a deep red woven wrap-cloak; signature prop a small wooden basket or a sprig of henna blossom.

payload.name: Daughters of Jerusalem
payload.note: The chorus of women of Jerusalem in Song of Solomon who speak and are addressed as a group, adjured by the bride; distinct from the friends who only send greetings in 3 John.

stages.label: Daughters of Jerusalem

quotes.quote: I am dark, but lovely, you daughters of Jerusalem
Go out, you daughters of Zion, and see King Solomon

stages.text: Daughters of Jerusalem: women of about eighteen to thirty years; slender to average build; warm olive-brown skin; dark hair worn long and bound or veiled in linen; modest, calm, attentive faces. Signature outfit: a long undyed linen tunic with a deep red woven wool cloak and a light veil over the hair. No personal props.

payload.name: Mother's house (Song of Solomon)
payload.note: The bride's mother's house where the lover wishes to bring her.

stages.label: Mother's house

quotes.quote: I would lead you, bringing you into the house of my mother, who would instruct me.
I would have you drink spiced wine, of the juice of my pomegranate.

stages.text: Mother's house: a modest village dwelling of pale limestone and mud brick under a flat roof, with a low doorway of dark timber and a courtyard wall. A pomegranate tree grows beside the house, heavy with fruit, and terraced vineyards and olive groves lie on the slopes behind it. Clay jars and a stone grinding place stand in the courtyard.

payload.title: Isaac and Abimelech in Gerar

payload.name: Isaac, son of Abraham and Sarah
payload.note: Son of Abraham and Sarah, husband of Rebekah and father of Esau and Jacob; the same Isaac across Genesis, Romans, Galatians, Hebrews and James, with the Genesis entry as the narrative core.

stages.label: Isaac

quotes.quote: When Isaac was old, and his eyes were dim, so that he could not see
Abraham took the wood of the burnt offering and laid it on Isaac his son.

stages.text: Isaac: a young man in late youth to middle age; lean, sturdy build from herding and labour in the open country; olive-brown skin; dark brown hair cut close at the neck, short beard kept trim; calm, steady face with heavy-lidded, grey-brown eyes that grow dim with age; wears a plain undyed linen tunic with a woollen wrap of earth-brown ochre, and leather sandals; carries a wooden staff of plain olive wood, and a bundle of kindling when bound to the wood at Moriah.

payload.name: Rebekah
payload.note: Wife of Isaac, sister of Laban, mother of Esau and Jacob, who schemes to secure the blessing for Jacob; the Genesis narrative and the Romans 9:10 reference both concern this same woman.

stages.label: Rebekah

quotes.quote: with her pitcher on her shoulder
the ring, and the bracelets on his sister’s hands
because she is beautiful to look at
jewels of silver, and jewels of gold, and clothing

stages.text: Rebekah: young woman in her late teens to early twenties when first met, slender and upright, fine-boned, with warm olive-brown skin, dark hair worn long and bound beneath a linen head-veil, dark luminous eyes and a calm, grave face. Her signature outfit is a dusty-rose wool tunic under an undyed ochre linen mantle, with simple sandals. Her signature props are a clay water pitcher carried on the shoulder and a silver-and-gold jewelled ring and bracelets.

payload.name: Abimelech of Gerar (Isaac's time)
payload.note: Philistine king of Gerar in Isaac's time who sees Isaac caressing Rebekah; a later holder of the Gerar title, shown in the Isaac narrative, not the Abraham-era king's own storyline.

stages.label: Abimelech of Gerar

quotes.quote: Isaac went to Abimelech king of the Philistines, to Gerar.
Abimelech king of the Philistines looked out at a window

stages.text: Abimelech of Gerar: man in his fifties, sturdy build, olive-brown skin, close-trimmed dark beard flecked with grey, lines at the eyes, dignified and watchful face. Signature outfit: a long undyed linen tunic under a deep blue woollen mantle with a narrow ochre border, leather sandals. Carries a plain bronze-headed staff of office.

payload.name: Gerar
payload.note: Philistine town where Abraham and Isaac sojourn and where Abimelech rules.

stages.label: Gerar

quotes.quote: He lived as a foreigner in Gerar.
Isaac departed from there, encamped in the valley of Gerar, and lived there.
The herdsmen of Gerar argued with Isaac’s herdsmen, saying, “The water is ours.”

stages.text: Gerar: a walled mud-brick town on a low rise above a broad valley in the dry southern land, with flat roofs, low gates and narrow lanes; around it stretch wells lined with stone, thorny acacia and tamarisk, dry grass and scattered terebinth trees, and open pasture beyond the fields.

payload.title: Peter on Jesus and David

payload.name: Simon Peter
payload.note: The fisherman apostle, first-called disciple and leader of the twelve, who appears in the Gospels, Acts, Galatians and both letters of Peter; all entries here are the same individual, distinguished only by role and portrayal.

stages.label: Simon Peter

quotes.quote: Simon, who is called Peter, and Andrew, his brother, casting a net into the sea; for they were fishermen.
You are Simon the son of Jonah. You shall be called Cephas

stages.text: Simon Peter: a sturdy man in his thirties, broad-shouldered from hauling nets, weathered brown skin from sun on the Sea of Galilee, short dark curly hair and a full beard flecked with grey. Plain undyed tunic of natural linen under a rough brown wool cloak. Signature props: a coiled fishing net over one shoulder and a wooden fishing staff.

payload.name: Crowd in Acts
payload.note: The crowd gathering in Jerusalem, Ephesus, Lystra and elsewhere to hear, mock or riot in Acts.

stages.label: Crowd in Acts

quotes.quote: the multitude came together and were bewildered, because everyone heard them speaking in his own language.
for the multitude of the people followed after, crying out, “Away with him!”

stages.text: Crowd in Acts: a typical member is an adult of about twenty to fifty years, lean and sun-browned from working outdoors, with dark brown or black hair worn short or tied back and beards kept short on men. Skin olive to tawny, faces weathered and serious. Clothing: a plain undyed linen tunic in ochre or earth-brown, a dark wool cloak in deep blue or grey, sandals. Carries no props of his own.

payload.title: Sabbath year, Sabbath day, and the three feasts

aliases: the mountain that might be touched
payload.name: Horeb/Mount Sinai
payload.note: The single mountain of God where the law and covenant are given; all listed entries (Exodus, Leviticus, Numbers, Deuteronomy, 1 Kings, Malachi, Hebrews) refer to the same mountain under the names Horeb, Sinai, God's mountain, referenced across divisions.

stages.label: Horeb/Mount Sinai

quotes.quote: All of Mount Sinai smoked, because Yahweh descended on it in fire
You shall set bounds to the people all around
the cloud covered it six days
The mountain burned with fire to the heart of the sky, with darkness, cloud, and thick darkness.

stages.text: Horeb/Mount Sinai: a single steep granite mountain rising from a stark desert wilderness of rock and sand; its lower slopes are broken boulders and gravel, its upper peak sharp and dark, with a cloud-wrapped summit. The base is marked by a rocky plain where the people camp, bounded by stones. No vegetation beyond scattered desert shrub; the mountain has no buildings.

payload.title: Proverbs on speech, wealth and justice
Asa's treaty with Ben Hadad

payload.name: Asa, king of Judah
payload.note: Son of Abijah and king of Judah who removes idols and makes a treaty with Ben Hadad of Syria against Baasha; the same king appears in 1 Kings and 2 Chronicles, so both entries belong to one cluster.

stages.label: Asa, king of Judah

quotes.quote: in the time of his old age he was diseased in his feet
Asa was diseased in his feet. His disease was exceedingly great

stages.text: Asa: man of mature years, lean and upright, in his forties to sixties; olive-brown skin; short dark beard with grey at the chin; black hair bound back under a plain linen headband; lined, earnest face with steady dark eyes; wears an undyed linen tunic and a deep blue wool royal cloak fastened at the shoulder with a bronze pin. Carries a plain staff of almond wood, a sign of age and his later infirmity.

aliases: Ben Hadad the king of Syria
payload.name: Ben Hadad, king of Syria (son of Tabrimmon)
payload.note: King of Syria at Damascus who makes treaties and wars with Israel and Judah in Kings and Chronicles, including the alliance with Asa; the Ben Hadad of Kings and Chronicles are the same king.

stages.label: Ben Hadad, king of Syria

quotes.quote: Ben Hadad the king of Syria gathered all his army together
Ben Hadad was drinking himself drunk in the pavilions
Ben Hadad fled and came into the city, into an inner room.

stages.text: Ben Hadad: a mature man in his late forties, broad-shouldered and strong, olive-bronze skin. Short dark curled beard trimmed close, hair bound back under a royal fillet. Stern, weathered face with a hooked nose and heavy brows. Signature outfit: a long embroidered tunic of deep crimson under a dark blue court robe with gold trim. Signature prop: a short gold-hilted sword at his belt.

payload.name: Baasha
payload.note: King of Israel who slew Nadab and reigned over the northern kingdom, fought Asa of Judah, and whose house Zimri destroyed; both entries are the same king, one in Kings and one in Chronicles.

stages.label: Baasha, king of Israel

quotes.quote: Baasha the son of Ahijah, of the house of Issachar, conspired against him
Baasha the son of Ahijah began to reign over all Israel in Tirzah for twenty-four years.

stages.text: Baasha: a man of about forty to fifty years; broad-shouldered and strong, of middle height; olive-brown skin; dark hair and a full, close-trimmed beard streaked with grey; a weathered, resolute face with deep-set eyes. Signature outfit: a long undertunic of undyed linen under a deep blue royal cloak fringed in gold, with a bronze-scaled military belt. Carries alone a plain iron-bladed sword in a leather scabbard.

payload.name: Ramah of Baasha's border
payload.note: Border town fortified by Baasha and dismantled by Asa in 1 Kings; a different place from Samuel's Ramah, known only from the treaty with Ben Hadad.

stages.label: Ramah of Baasha's border

quotes.quote: Baasha king of Israel went up against Judah, and built Ramah
They carried away the stones of Ramah, and its timber

stages.text: Ramah: a fortified hill town on a limestone ridge in the border country between Israel and Judah, north of Jerusalem. Its walls are of rough-hewn stone laid in courses, with a gate tower of dressed masonry and timber beams, its roofs flat and plastered. Terraced olive groves and terebinth trees cover the slopes, with scrub oak and wild thyme on the rocky ground.

payload.title: Abraham justified by faith

aliases: my child's father in the faith
the aged prisoner of Christ Jesus
payload.name: Paul the apostle
payload.note: The apostle Paul, author and speaker of all thirteen letters; the same individual across Romans, Corinthians, Galatians, Ephesians, Philippians, Colossians, Thessalonians, Timothy, Titus and Philemon, identified by his apostolic authorship and first-person voice.

stages.label: Paul the apostle

quotes.quote: being such a one as Paul, the aged, but also a prisoner of Jesus Christ.
I, Paul, write this greeting with my own hand. Remember my chains.
I, Paul, write this with my own hand

stages.text: Paul the apostle: man of middle to later years, perhaps fifties to sixties, wiry and weathered from travel and imprisonment; Jewish Mediterranean features, olive-brown skin, short greying-dark beard and close-cropped hair receding at the temples; lined brow, steady dark eyes. Signature outfit: plain undyed wool tunic in ochre-brown under a dark-blue cloak. Signature prop: a rolled parchment scroll and a reed pen case at the belt.

payload.title: Counsel and decree against Vashti

payload.name: Ahasuerus
payload.note: King of Persia and Media who deposes Vashti and marries Esther.

stages.label: Ahasuerus, King of Persia and Media

quotes.quote: wearing the royal crown, to show the people and the princes her beauty
this is Ahasuerus who reigned from India even to Ethiopia
The king took off his ring, which he had taken from Haman
except those to whom the king might hold out the golden scepter

stages.text: Ahasuerus: man in his middle years, broad-shouldered and upright; dark, neatly curled beard and hair under a royal crown of gold; olive-brown skin; calm, heavy-lidded, dignified face. Signature outfit: long layered royal robe of deep purple and gold-embroidered blue over a white tunic. Signature props: a gold signet ring and a golden scepter.

payload.name: Memucan
payload.note: One of the seven princes of Persia and Media who advises the king to depose Vashti.

stages.label: Memucan

quotes.quote: the seven princes of Persia and Media, who saw the king’s face, and sat first in the kingdom

stages.text: Memucan: a man in his fifties, of middling height and sturdy build; olive-brown skin; short dark hair and a neatly trimmed dark beard flecked with grey; a composed, sober face with deep-set eyes. Signature outfit: a long pleated court robe of deep blue wool edged with gold braid, with a close-fitting cap of the same blue. Carries a slender gold-tipped staff of office.

payload.name: the seven princes of Persia and Media
payload.note: Counsellors who sit first in the kingdom and are consulted about Vashti.

stages.label: Seven princes of Persia and Media

quotes.quote: the seven princes of Persia and Media, who saw the king’s face, and sat first in the kingdom

stages.text: Seven princes of Persia and Media: mature men in their forties to fifties; sturdy, upright build; olive-brown skin; full dark beards trimmed square; grave, dignified faces with deep-set eyes. Signature outfit: long layered court robe of deep blue wool with a gold-embroidered border, a tall felt cap, and a gold torque at the neck. Carry a short ceremonial staff of dark wood tipped with gold.

payload.name: Palace at Susa
payload.note: The royal palace in Susa of Ahasuerus, site of the feast, Vashti's refusal, and Esther's queenship; distinguish by its Persian setting in Susa.

stages.label: Palace at Susa

quotes.quote: Esther put on her royal clothing and stood in the inner court of the king’s house, next to the king’s house.
The king sat on his royal throne in the royal house, next to the entrance of the house.
The king arose in his wrath from the banquet of wine and went into the palace garden.
whoever, whether man or woman, comes to the king into the inner court without being called

stages.text: Palace at Susa: a vast Persian royal complex on a raised platform of sun-baked brick above the plain of Susa; tall columned halls of cedar and stone with painted glazed brick friezes in blue, ochre and white; a great gate with winged guardian figures; an inner court paved in pale stone; the king's house with a throne room near its entrance; a walled palace garden of date palms, plane trees, pools and channels of water.

aliases: the kingdom from India to Ethiopia
payload.name: the provinces
payload.note: The 127 provinces of the empire where decrees are sent and the Jews live.

stages.label: the provinces

quotes.quote: the governors and princes of the provinces which are from India to Ethiopia, one hundred twenty-seven provinces
the army of Persia and Media, the nobles and princes of the provinces

stages.text: the provinces: a vast realm of 127 provinces spanning from India to Ethiopia; wide river plains, dry steppe and desert, date palms and tamarisk along irrigation canals, walled cities of sun-dried brick and stone with gates, royal roads with milestones, Persian palaces with columned halls, and village settlements of mudbrick houses.
